info.title: Chat Service
info.description: Multi-org AI chat service. Streams Gemini AI responses via SSE with configurable system prompts and built-in workflow tools.

sessionId.description: The session UUID — store this for subsequent requests

content.description: Incremental text fragment of the AI response

thinking.description: Incremental fragment of the model's internal reasoning

id.description: Unique identifier (format: tc_<uuid>) — use this to match with the corresponding tool_result

args.description: Input arguments passed to the tool, as a JSON object

id.description: Matches the id from the corresponding tool_call event

name.description: The tool name that produced this result

result.description: The tool output — can be a string or a JSON object

input_type.description: The type of input widget the frontend should render

placeholder.description: Placeholder text for the input field

field.description: Identifier for what the input represents

value.description: Pre-filled value for the input field. When present, the frontend renders the field already populated so the user can confirm with a single click. When absent, the field is empty.
value.example: Automated cold email outreach campaign targeting SaaS founders

value.description: Text to send as the next user message when the button is clicked

buttons.description: Quick-reply buttons extracted from the AI response

code.description: Machine-readable error code. `model_overloaded` — Claude is temporarily at capacity (retry after a moment). `rate_limited` — too many requests (respect retry-after). `model_error` — transient upstream error. `internal_error` — unexpected server error. `session_not_found` — the supplied sessionId does not exist or belongs to another user.

message.description: Human-readable error message explaining what went wrong
message.example: Claude is temporarily overloaded. Please try again in a moment.

inputTokens.description: Context size: input tokens of the turn's LAST model call (post-compaction for Anthropic, post-trim for Gemini). Never the turn's summed input: each tool round re-sends the whole prompt.

outputTokens.description: Tokens generated by the model on this turn.

maxTokens.description: Upper bound on the input window the service is willing to use, in tokens (200000 — Anthropic Sonnet limit, also enforced for Gemini).

percent.description: inputTokens / maxTokens as a 0–100 integer, capped at 100. Use this to render a usage gauge.

SSEChoicesEvent.description: Rich clickable cards from the `present_choices` tool. Terminates the AI's turn (like input_request): send the clicked card's `value` as the next /chat message. Also stored on the assistant message (`choices`) so GET /sessions/* re-renders it.

description.example: They replied yesterday and are waiting.

value.description: What the client sends back as the next user message when the card is clicked. Equals `label` when the model gave none.

icon.description: Icon name the client maps to its icon set (e.g. 'mail', 'rocket', 'users').

value.description: The big figure, exactly as a tool served it (the model never computes a stat).

series.description: Tiny sparkline series, oldest first, values as a tool served them.

ChoiceVisual.description: Optional visual on a choice card: an icon, a logo/image, a big number with unit, or a tiny chart.

question.example: What do you want to do first?

allowFreeText.description: Whether the client keeps the free-text box as an escape hatch (true unless the model said false).

SSEOpenPageEvent.description: The `open_page` tool asks the client to open a dashboard page in its side panel. The client resolves `page` (+ ids) to a URL. Does not end the turn. Stored on the assistant message (`openPages`).

page.description: Page identifier the CLIENT resolves to a URL (its list is given to the model in the config's system prompt). Never a URL.

title.description: Optional short caption for the panel (why it opened).

model.description: Model alias. Null means provider default (sonnet for anthropic, flash-pro for google).

supportKind.description: Support function every /chat turn under this config serves. Null means the turn rides its caller's run.

key.description: Config key — identifies which chat mode this config is for (e.g. 'workflow', 'feature', 'press-kit'). Each org can have multiple configs, one per key.

systemPrompt.description: System prompt sent to the LLM for this chat mode
systemPrompt.example: You are an AI assistant that helps users understand and modify their workflows.

allowedTools.description: List of tool names the LLM is allowed to use in this chat mode. Only these tools will be provided to the model and executable server-side. Available tools: request_user_input, create_workflow, upgrade_workflow, fork_workflow, validate_workflow, get_workflow_details, get_workflow_required_providers, list_workflows, get_prompt_template, update_prompt_template, list_services, list_service_endpoints, list_org_keys, get_key_source, list_key_sources, check_provider_requirements, create_feature, update_feature, list_features, get_feature, get_feature_inputs, prefill_feature, get_feature_stats, update_campaign_fields, extract_brand_fields, browse_url

content.description: Raw text response from the model. WARNING: when responseFormat is "json", this field may contain markdown code fences (e.g. ```json...```). Do NOT use this field for JSON parsing — use the `json` field instead.

json.description: Parsed JSON object — present when responseFormat is "json". IMPORTANT: always use this field (not `content`) when you need structured data. Markdown fences are already stripped and the JSON is pre-parsed. If the model returns non-parsable JSON, the endpoint returns 502 instead of silently omitting this field.

model.description: Versioned model ID actually used for the completion (resolved by the service from the provider+model alias)

from.description: Versioned model ID the caller asked for.

reason.description: `out_of_credit`: the asked model's provider has no credit on our account. `rate_limited`: it still answered 429 after the retry budget. `quota_exhausted`: it refused for a per-day / per-hour cap or asked for a wait longer than the retries (OPEN-LLM-FREE-1124).

fallback.description: Present only when the requested model's provider could not serve on our platform key (no credit, a rate limit that outlasted the retries, an exhausted quota) and the call was served by another vendor's model: the cheapest of the same tier that takes the request (VENDOR-CREDIT-1030, LLM-CREDIT-GENERIC-1108). `model` is then the fallback that ran, and the run declares the fallback's own cost names.

brandToolCalls.description: Present only with `brandTools` and a brand that has a server plugged: how many brand tool calls the model made before answering.

error.description: Why billing refused the spend. "Insufficient credits" = the balance (adding credit helps). "Sales funnel max budget reached" / "... unreadable" = the campaign's max budget refused it whatever the balance: adding credit cannot help, raising the campaign's max budget can.

balance_cents.description: Current credit balance in USD cents

required_cents.description: Estimated cost of this request in USD cents

reason.description: billing-service's refusal reason, verbatim. Present only when a sales funnel max budget refused the spend, absent on a balance refusal.

sales_funnel_cap.description: The cap that refused the spend, verbatim from billing-service; present only with `reason`.

message.description: The prompt to send to the LLM
message.example: Given this brand context, generate 10 Google search queries for PR outreach.

systemPrompt.description: Inline system prompt — no pre-registered config required. Empty string is allowed: the provider receives no system prompt and falls back to its default behavior. The value is forwarded byte-equal to the provider; the service does not inject, enrich, or nudge the prompt.
systemPrompt.example: You are a PR research assistant.

responseFormat.description: Set to "json" to instruct the model to return valid JSON. The response will be parsed and returned in the `json` field.

responseSchema.description: Optional JSON Schema describing the exact shape of the expected JSON response. When set, the schema is passed to the provider's structured-output API (Gemini: `generationConfig.responseSchema`; Anthropic: `output_config.format` with `type: "json_schema"`) and the provider enforces the shape server-side. Implies `responseFormat: "json"`. **Anthropic constraint:** the schema must be strict — `additionalProperties: false` and an explicit `properties` map. Permissive schemas are rejected with 400.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature (0–2). Lower = more deterministic. Rejected with a 400 by the reasoning-first models that removed the sampling parameters — today `anthropic`/`fable` (Claude Fable 5.2) and `openai`/`gpt-pro` (GPT-6 Astra). The request is refused before any cost is held; the parameter is never silently dropped.

maxTokens.description: Optional output-token budget for this call. When set, it caps the provider's generation (Anthropic `max_tokens` / Gemini `maxOutputTokens`, bounded to 64000) AND sizes the pre-call cost reservation exactly to this budget. Omit it and the service reserves a right-sized estimate (well below the 64000 model max) while the provider keeps the full budget so long outputs are not truncated. Declare it when you know your output is small (e.g. scoring, short JSON, suggestion lists) — this prevents a burst of concurrent calls from over-reserving against your org balance.

provider.description: LLM provider to use. `anthropic` and `google` are native clients with the full feature set (vision, web search, thinking controls). `deepseek`, `zai` (Z.ai / GLM), `moonshot` (Kimi), `openai` (GPT) are called directly over their OpenAI-compatible APIs by one shared adapter — text in / text out only, opt-in per call, no existing caller reaches them implicitly. Each vendor resolves its OWN API key from key-service under this exact slug.

model.description:
**Preferred: an LLM dynasty slug** (one vendor line, its versions pooled; the full list with versions is `GET /internal/model-dynasties`). The slug always runs the dynasty's head (newest served version): anthropic → claude-haiku|claude-sonnet|claude-opus|claude-fable, google → gemini-flash-lite|gemini-flash|gemini-pro, deepseek → deepseek-flash, zai → glm-flash|glm, moonshot → kimi-k2|kimi-k3, openai → gpt-astra|gpt-sol|gpt-terra. The head's exact model id (e.g. `gemini-4-hydrogen`) is also accepted, to pin that version. Spend is declared under the concrete model that ran, whatever name called it.

Legacy aliases (version-free, each a redirect to its dynasty's head):

**anthropic:** `haiku` → Claude Haiku 5.5 (fast/cheap), `sonnet` → Claude Sonnet 5.5 (balanced), `opus` → Claude Opus 5.5 (high quality), `fable` → Claude Fable 5.2, the tier above Opus (1M context, always-on reasoning). `sonnet`, `opus` and `fable` reject `temperature` with a 400 — Anthropic removed the sampling parameters on its always-thinking models, as OpenAI did on its GPT models. On `sonnet` and `opus`, `disableThinking: true` minimizes reasoning (effort `low`); thinking cannot be fully disabled there.
**google:** `flash-lite` and `flash` → Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite (cheapest, vision), `flash-pro` → Gemini 3.8 Flash (mid-tier), `pro` → Gemini 3.1 Pro (most powerful).
**deepseek:** `deepseek-flash` → DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1M context, 2500 concurrent requests). `deepseek-pro` is a **deprecated synonym** resolving to the same model: DeepSeek discontinued V4 Pro on 2026-09-14 and routes it to V4.1 Flash at the Flash price. Prefer `deepseek-flash`.
**zai:** `glm-flash` → `glm-5.3-flash` (fast, cheap, 50 concurrent requests), `glm-pro` → `glm-5.3` (flagship, 15 concurrent requests).
**moonshot:** `kimi-flash` → `kimi-k2.6` (value tier), `kimi-pro` → `kimi-k3` (flagship, 1M context).
**openai:** `gpt-pro` → GPT-6 Astra (flagship; 1.05M context, 128k output, always-on reasoning floored at `low`), `gpt-sol` → GPT-6 Sol, `gpt-terra` → GPT-5.6 Terra (the latest Terra; there is no GPT-6 Terra). On `gpt-sol` / `gpt-terra`, `disableThinking: true` turns reasoning fully off. All three reject `temperature`.
A call the vendor refuses for a rate limit or a quota is served by the next model of the fallback order (`fallback.reason`).

The direct-vendor providers are **text only**: `imageUrl` and `webSearch` are rejected with 400.

The model must match the provider: anthropic → haiku|sonnet|opus|fable, google → flash-lite|flash|flash-pro|pro, deepseek → deepseek-flash|deepseek-pro, zai → glm-flash|glm-pro, moonshot → kimi-flash|kimi-pro, openai → gpt-pro|gpt-sol|gpt-terra.

webSearch.description: Opt-in native web search. When true, the resolved provider answers using its OWN native web search — Google Search grounding for `google`, the server-side `web_search` tool for `anthropic` — so the response reflects live web content instead of the model's parametric memory. Citation source URLs are appended to `content` (text mode only). Omitted or false = no grounding, byte-identical to a non-grounded call (no extra cost). The web-search cost is metered per query/search and billed in addition to tokens.

disableThinking.description: Minimize the model's internal reasoning ("thinking") so the whole output budget goes to the answer. Use for extraction / structured-JSON / scoring tasks that don't need chain-of-thought. Effect is provider-floored, NOT a guaranteed full-off (like `maxSearches`): Gemini 2.5 → thinking fully OFF; Anthropic: `sonnet` / `opus` (Claude Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5, whose thinking cannot be disabled) → effort `low`, `haiku` / `fable` → no-op; Gemini 3 has NO full-off, so it drops to the lowest level THAT MODEL allows — `minimal` on the Flash-Lite models, `low` on Pro and on the `flash-pro` default (Gemini 3.8 Flash, which rejects `minimal`). On the direct vendors (`deepseek`, `zai`, `moonshot`) reasoning goes fully OFF — on `openai` it goes fully OFF for `gpt-sol` / `gpt-terra` and to the lowest effort GPT-6 Astra accepts (`low`) for `gpt-pro`, since that model has no full-off — and that is ALREADY the default for any request asking for structured output (a `responseSchema` or `responseFormat: "json"`) — those callers parse the object and never see the reasoning, which is billed as output tokens (measured 2026-08-25: GLM-5.2 703 → 389 output tokens, Kimi K2.6 1,173 → 452, same answers). Pass `false` to keep reasoning ON for a structured request; pass `true` to turn it off for a free-text one. Omitted = the service default (bounded thinking on the native providers, byte-identical to a normal call; reasoning off for structured vendor calls, provider-normal for text ones). A vendor model that refuses the option fails loud with a 400 in its own words rather than silently reasoning anyway.

thinkingLevel.description: Optional per-call Gemini-3 thinking level — the same graduated levels the /chat config path supports. Lets a caller dial reasoning effort without changing the model. Precedence: `disableThinking` (when set) always wins → the provider floor, ignoring this field. Otherwise the model generates at this level. Omitted = the service default ("low"), byte-identical to a normal call (existing callers see ZERO change). Applies only to Gemini-3 models; a safe no-op on Gemini 2.5 (uses its bounded budget) and Anthropic (use `effort` there). Example use: an extraction task asks for "low" — cheaper/faster than default but above the floor.

effort.description: Optional per-call Anthropic thinking effort (`low` | `medium` | `high` | `xhigh` | `max`). When set, the model reasons at that level for this one call (sent as adaptive thinking + `output_config.effort`); works with `responseSchema`. Thinking tokens are billed as output tokens and are included in `tokensOutput`. Omitted = byte-identical to a call without it (no thinking block is sent). Anthropic only (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`): with any other provider, or beside `disableThinking: true`, the request is refused with a 400. Gemini callers use `thinkingLevel`.

imageUrl.description: URL of an image to include in the prompt. The image is fetched server-side and sent to the model as a visual input. Supported by all models, but recommended with provider: "google", model: "flash-lite" for cost-effective vision tasks (image classification, scoring, analysis).

alt.description: Alt text of the image (from the HTML img tag)

title.description: Title attribute or caption of the image

sourceUrl.description: The page URL where the image was found (not the image URL itself)

imageContext.description: Optional metadata about the image (alt text, title, source page). Injected into the prompt alongside the image to help the model classify and score it more accurately. Only meaningful when imageUrl is provided.

brandTools.description: Opt-in (BRAND-MCP-1109): run this call with the brand's own MCP tools (the servers the brand plugged under `/orgs/brands/{brandId}/mcp-servers`). The model may call them (read and write) in a bounded tool loop, then answers in this request's `responseSchema` (or text): the response has the same shape as without it, plus `brandToolCalls`. Each tool call is an event `brand-mcp-tool-call` on the call's run; every LLM round is declared on the run. Served on every provider (`anthropic` through its own tool-use loop, `google`, `deepseek`, `zai`, `moonshot`, `openai`), with `webSearch` and `imageUrl` where the plain call serves them; the one refusal (400, before any spend) is `webSearch` on `google` with it: Gemini cannot ground on Google Search and call tools in one request. A brand with no server plugged runs the plain one-shot call. Omitted = byte-identical to before. The brand belongs to `x-org-id`.

url.description: Cloudflare-hosted URL for the generated image. Store and serve this URL; generated bytes are not returned.

mimeType.description: MIME type for the stored generated image.

model.description: Versioned Gemini image model used by chat-service.

tokensInput.description: Input tokens reported by Gemini for the prompt.

tokensOutput.description: Image output tokens reported by Gemini.

text.description: Optional text part returned alongside the image, when Gemini includes one.

prompt.description: Text prompt for Gemini image generation. Chat-service owns provider/model request shaping; callers should describe the desired image, not pass Gemini generationConfig fields.
prompt.example: Generate a square PNG avatar portrait for a B2B SaaS buyer persona: confident marketing leader, clean studio lighting, no text.

size.description: Generated image size. Omit for `small` (512px). `medium` maps to 1K, `large` maps to 2K, and `xlarge` maps to 4K.

aspectRatio.description: Width:height of the generated image, enforced by the provider (not the prompt). Omit for `1:1` (square).

runId.description: The platform run that carried this call in runs-service (the child of `x-run-id` when sent). Its cost is this call's whole spend.

message.description: The prompt to send to the LLM
message.example: Analyze this workflow definition and suggest field mappings.

systemPrompt.description: Inline system prompt. Empty string is allowed: the provider receives no system prompt and falls back to its default behavior. The value is forwarded byte-equal to the provider; the service does not inject, enrich, or nudge the prompt.

model.description: Provider model id that transcribes (or transcribed) the file.

url.description: Source URL WITHOUT its query string.

languages.description: Completed only. ISO 639-1 codes spoken, in order of first appearance (`["en","fr"]`); empty when nothing is spoken; null when the model did not state them (never guessed).

durationSeconds.description: Completed only. Length of the video as the provider decoded it (null for audio or when not reported).

segments.description: Completed only. One entry per sentence or short group of sentences, in order.

text.description: Completed only. Every segment's text, one per line.

error.description: Failed only. Why, as a code and in words.

runId.description: Platform run carrying the declared cost.

startSeconds.description: Where this passage starts in the recording, in seconds.

text.description: The words spoken, verbatim, in the language spoken (never translated).

TranscriptionErrorCode.description: `source_unreachable` the URL failed or expired · `source_size_unknown` no Content-Length/Content-Range · `file_too_large` over 2 GB · `not_media` not a video/audio type · `upload_failed` transfer to the provider failed · `unreadable_media` the provider could not decode the file · `provider_refused` the model call failed · `transcript_truncated` the output limit was hit before the end · `unparseable_transcript` the model answered something that is not a timed transcript · `interrupted` a service restart cut the job (start it again).

url.description: HTTPS GET URL of the video or audio file (a presigned bucket URL is fine; it must stay valid for the whole job, ~10 min for 2 GB). Range requests are used for the check; the file is then streamed once. Max 2 GB. The query string (signature) is never stored.

post.summary: Synchronous LLM completion
post.description:
One-shot, non-streaming LLM call for service-to-service use. Returns a JSON response with the model output.

Unlike POST /chat, this endpoint:
- Does **not** create or use sessions (stateless, one-shot)
- Accepts an inline `systemPrompt` (no pre-registered config required)
- Returns JSON instead of SSE
- Supports `responseFormat: "json"` — when set, the parsed object is returned in the `json` field (always use `json`, not `content`, for structured data)
- Supports optional `temperature` override
- Supports **vision** via the `imageUrl` field — the image is fetched server-side and sent as visual input to the model

**Provider + model (both required):**
Callers specify a provider and a version-free model alias. The service resolves the latest versioned model ID internally.

| provider | model | Description |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| `anthropic` | `sonnet` | General-purpose, high quality |
| `anthropic` | `haiku` | Faster/cheaper for simple extraction and classification |
| `anthropic` | `opus` | Highest quality for complex reasoning |
| `google` | `flash-lite` | Cheapest, cost-effective vision model for image analysis |
| `google` | `flash` | Balanced price-performance with reasoning capabilities |
| `google` | `pro` | Most powerful Google model for complex tasks |

All Google models require a Google API key configured in key-service (provider: `google`).

**When the vendor cannot serve on our platform key (OPEN-LLM-FREE-1124):** an empty balance, a 429 that outlasts the retries, or a quota (a per-day / per-hour cap, a Retry-After longer than the retries) moves the call to the next model of the fallback order; the response carries `fallback: {from, reason}` (`out_of_credit | rate_limited | quota_exhausted`) and the run declares the model that ran. No model left = `502 {code: "no_serving_model"}`. An org's own key keeps the vendor's 429. A provider with no platform key registered answers `503 {code: "platform_key_missing", provider}`.

**Use cases:** generating search queries, scoring/analyzing text, image classification and scoring (with `imageUrl` + google/flash-lite), any service that needs a quick LLM call without conversation context.

post.summary: Platform-level LLM completion (no billing, no run tracking)
post.description:
Internal endpoint for platform-level LLM calls that do not belong to a specific org or user.

**Auth:** Requires only `x-api-key` (no `x-org-id` or `x-user-id`).

**On behalf of a caller's run:** send that run's id in `x-run-id` and the platform run opened here becomes its child, so the cost reaches the outcome the caller produced. The response's `runId` names the run that carried the call.

**Whose work (required):** send the caller's run in `x-run-id` (the spend rides the outcome that run produces), OR, when no run stands behind the call, declare the support function in the body: `support: {kind, reason}`, kind one of `payment_fees | brand_setup | copilot | platform_llm | staff_experiment | product_feature | retired_product` (reported apart, never on an outcome). Both at once = 400. Neither = 400, before any spend.

**Key resolution:** Uses the platform key directly via `GET /keys/platform/{provider}/decrypt` — no org-level key lookup.

**When the vendor cannot serve on our platform key (OPEN-LLM-FREE-1124):** an empty balance, a 429 that outlasts the retries, or a quota (a per-day / per-hour cap, a Retry-After longer than the retries) moves the call to the next model of the fallback order; the response carries `fallback: {from, reason}` (`out_of_credit | rate_limited | quota_exhausted`) and the run declares the model that ran. No model left = `502 {code: "no_serving_model"}`. An org's own key keeps the vendor's 429. A provider with no platform key registered answers `503 {code: "platform_key_missing", provider}`.

**No org billing.** Spend is declared on a platform run (platform-billed). This endpoint is for internal service-to-service calls (e.g. workflow upgrades at startup) where there is no org to bill and no user-initiated run to track.

Does not support `imageUrl` or `imageContext` — use `POST /complete` for vision tasks.

**Whose work (required):** send the caller's run in `x-run-id` (the platform run becomes its child: the spend rides the outcome that run produces), OR, when no run stands behind the call, declare the support function in the body: `support: {kind, reason}`, kind one of `payment_fees | brand_setup | copilot | platform_llm | staff_experiment | product_feature | retired_product` (reported apart, never on an outcome). Poll `GET /internal/platform-transcriptions/{id}` (every 10-30 s) until `status` is `completed` or `failed`: a 5 min phone video takes ~1-2 min, a 1 GB / 15 min one a few minutes.

**What comes back:** the words spoken, verbatim (no translation, summary or cleanup), in the language spoken; mixed languages keep each part in its own. One segment per sentence or short group of sentences, each with its start time.

Later failures land on the job as `error.code`.

**Auth:** `x-api-key` only (no org, no user).

**Spend:** declared on a platform run (`costSource: "platform"`) under the model's Gemini token cost names (e.g. `google-flash-lite-3.5-tokens-input` / `-tokens-output`), as `actual` once the model answered (even when the answer is then refused as truncated).

post.description:
Starts the transcription of the video or audio file at `url` (up to 4 GB, 1-2 h interviews) and **answers at once** with **202** and the transcription (`status: "downloading"`). Then poll `GET /orgs/media-transcriptions/{id}`.

**Your outcome, your Unit:** chat-service declares NO outcome and NO Unit for a transcription. The caller's run declares it, with `subjectService: "chat-service"` and `subjectId` = the transcription `id` (stable, never reused).

**Idempotency:** with an `idempotencyKey` this org already used, the answer is that transcription (**200**), whatever its status, and nothing is started. A retry after `failed` needs a NEW key.

**Errors, nothing started:** 422 `source_unreachable` (also a URL that is not on the public internet) / `source_size_unknown` / `not_media`, 413 `file_too_large` (over 4 GB), 503 `box_transcriber_not_configured`.

post.summary: Stream AI chat response
post.description:
Send a message and receive a streamed AI response via Server-Sent Events (SSE).

**Config resolution:**
The `configKey` field selects which chat config to use. Resolution order:
1. Per-org config: `(orgId, configKey)` from PUT /config
2. Platform config: `(configKey)` from PUT /platform-config
3. If neither exists → 404

The selected config determines both the system prompt and which tools the LLM can use.

**Session lifecycle:**
- To start a new conversation, omit `sessionId` (or pass `null`). The first SSE event will be `{"sessionId":"<uuid>"}` — store this ID.
- To continue a conversation, pass that `sessionId` in subsequent requests.
- To reset a conversation (e.g. after a fork), omit `sessionId` and send a new `context`.

**Context:**
The `context` field is a free-form JSON object provided by the frontend on **every** message. It is injected into the system prompt but not stored. Re-send it on every request — the service does not cache it. After a fork (e.g. workflow updated → new workflow created), the frontend should update its context with the new IDs and either continue the session or start a new one.

**SSE event order:**
Each `data:` line contains a JSON object. Events arrive in this order:

1. **Session** — `{"sessionId":"<uuid>"}` (always first)
2. **Thinking** _(optional)_ — `thinking_start` → one or more `thinking_delta` → `thinking_stop`.
3. **Tokens** — `{"type":"token","content":"..."}` streamed incrementally.
4. **Tool calls** _(optional, repeatable)_ — `tool_call` followed by `tool_result`, then more thinking/tokens.
5. **Open page** _(optional, repeatable)_ — `{"type":"open_page","page":"...",brandId?,offerId?,campaignId?,audienceId?,leadId?,title?}` when the AI wants the client to open a dashboard page in its side panel (config allows `open_page`). Does not end the turn. No `tool_call`/`tool_result` pair is streamed for it.
6. **Input request** _(optional)_ — `input_request` when the AI needs structured user input (terminates the response).
7. **Choices** _(optional)_ — `{"type":"choices","question"?,"choices":[{label,description?,value,visual?}],"allowFreeText"}` rich clickable cards (config allows `present_choices`). Terminates the response; send the clicked card's `value` as the next message. No `tool_call`/`tool_result` pair is streamed for it. `visual` is one of `{type:"icon",icon}`, `{type:"image",imageUrl}`, `{type:"number",value,unit?}`, `{type:"chart",series,unit?}`.
8. **Buttons** _(optional)_ — `{"type":"buttons","buttons":[...]}` with quick-reply options, sent after all tokens.
9. **Context usage** — `context_usage` context size of the turn's last model call.
10. **Error** _(optional)_ — `{"type":"error","message":"..."}` if something goes wrong. Sent before `[DONE]`.
11. **Done** — `"[DONE]"` (always last).

Choices and opened pages are persisted on the assistant message and returned by GET /sessions/{sessionId} and GET /sessions/latest (`choices`, `openPages`).

**Available tools** depend on the config's `allowedTools`. The LLM only sees and can call the tools listed there. See PUT /config documentation for the full list of available tool names.

post.summary: Score documents against a brand profile (semantic similarity)
post.description:
RAG-style semantic similarity scoring for picking the best document(s) for a brand.

Used by journalists-quotes-service to rank quote requests against a brand profile, and by any other consumer that needs cheap document-vs-brand scoring.

**Multi-brand:** accepts `brandIds: string[]` (1..5) for joint scoring across multiple brands. Legacy `brandId: string` is still accepted and is equivalent to `brandIds: [brandId]`. When both are provided, `brandIds` wins. At least one is required. Multi-brand calls compute ONE embedding against the consolidated brand profile (brand-service merges field values across input brands) and ONE score per document.

**Pipeline:**
1. Canonical-sort `brandIds` ascending.
2. Resolve consolidated brand context via brand-service (industry, expertise, target audience, voice) in ONE call.
3. Synthesize a brand-profile query string (or use the caller-supplied `query`).
4. Compute the brand-profile embedding via Gemini's `gemini-embedding-001` (cached per (orgId, sorted(brandIds), contentHash)).
5. Compute embeddings for each `documents[i].text` in a single batch call.
6. Score = cosine similarity, sorted descending.

**Caching:** the brand-profile embedding is cached per canonical-sorted brand set + content hash. Same brand set, same resolved fields → cache hit. Different brand set (even subset) → cache miss. The cache automatically invalidates when any resolved brand field changes.

**Volume:** designed for batches up to 100 documents per request, up to 5 brands per joint profile.

post.summary: Ask typed questions about text or an image and get calibrated answers
post.description:
Answers one or more TYPED questions about a piece of state, each with the model's own probability distribution: a yes-probability for a `noul`, a picked option plus a full distribution and a `confidence` for a `choice`, a weighted position on ordered levels for a `score`.

Backed by a typed JUDGE, never a text generator. `judge` picks it: `jev` (TypeSafe Jev 1.13, the default), `openai-luna` (OpenAI Decisions API, gpt-6-luna), `cloudflare-clef` or `cloudflare-clef-flash` (Cloudflare Workers AI). No fallback between judges.

**Images:** send `image.url` (PNG/JPEG over https) with or without `state`, and ask the question about what the image shows. The service downloads it once, fits it to the judges' limits (longest side 1568 px, aspect kept; a side under 280 px padded; source up to 16 MiB) and sends every judge the same pixels. Image tokens bill at the judge's input rate. An unusable image (dead URL, not an image, too big) is a 400 before any spend.

**Why this is not `/complete`:** that route returns prose the caller parses, and tells it nothing about how sure the model was. A consumer that FREEZES a classification at write time needs the certainty to decide whether to freeze at all — so nothing here reduces an answer to its winning value. Read `confidence` (or the `noul` probability itself) and route a hesitant answer to your own "unknown" state.

**Pipeline:**
1. Fetch and fit the image, if any. Resolve the judge's key via key-service.
2. Provision + authorize the input-token spend, then call the vendor.
3. Reconcile the hold to the EXACT input-token count the vendor reports.

**Billing:** input tokens only, at the judge's own rate (Jev: `typesafe-jev-1.13-tokens-input`; Luna: `openai-gpt-6-luna-decisions-tokens-input`, the long-context row past 272K prompt tokens). Neither judge charges for output, so nothing here declares an output cost.

**Limits:** 64k tokens per request overall, 32k for the state plus the longest single question; at most 255 options per Choice; 2-10 levels per Score. A request over the token budget is refused by the vendor and surfaces as a 400 carrying its words.

post.description:
The org-less twin of `POST /orgs/judgments`: same body, same typed answers with their probability distributions intact. Use it from a caller that has no org to bill — a cron, a poller, a backfill, a platform classifier.

**Identity:** service auth only (`x-api-key`). No `x-org-id`, no `x-user-id`.

**On behalf of a caller's run:** send that run's id in `x-run-id` and the platform run opened here becomes its child, so the cost reaches the outcome the caller produced. Never fabricate one: an unknown run is refused (400). The response's `runId` names the run that carried the call.

Both at once = 400. Neither = 400, before any spend.

**Billing:** the judge's PLATFORM key, declared on a platform run under the same input-token cost name as the org route. There is no org balance to gate on, so there is no affordability check and no provisioned hold — the only quantity ever declared is the exact input-token count the vendor reports. Output is free at this vendor, so nothing declares an output cost.

Everything else — the pinned release on the wire, the refusal to flatten an answer to its winning value, the retry schedule — is identical to the org-scoped route.
